Global Health Development (GHD) is a regional initiative created to support countries in the
Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR) and to strengthen their health systems to respond to
public health challenges and threats. GHD was initiated to advance the work of the Eastern
Mediterranean Public Health Network (EMPHNET) by building coordinating mechanisms with
Ministries of Health, International Organizations, and other institutions to improve population
health outcomes. Serving as a collaborative platform, GHD|EMPHNET is dedicated to serving
the region by supporting efforts to promote public health policies, strategic planning,
sustainable financing, resource mobilization, public health programs, and other related
services.

Introduction
This manual compiles policies and procedures for organizing, running, and closing
events. The actual technical content of the event is set aside as the manual’s  main
purpose is to focus on the management aspect of events.
Events at GHD|EMPHNET may take several forms that vary  in complexity and
arrangement requirements. However, the running of all these event s shall include
planning, preparation, conduct, and closeout.
For the purpose of this manual , an Event is defined as Assessment, Field Outreach,
Meeting, Regional Meeting, National /sub-national or Regional Training Workshop or
another Training Event, as well as Conferences/Symposia, where:
• Regional/Global Conferences and/or Scientific Symposia: These regional/
global events require extensive planning, preparation, implementation, and
closeout efforts. While general elements of this manual are applicable to e ach
of such high-level events, they may come with their own guidance/guideline as
needed. (Conference details are covered in separate document).
• Regional training workshop: Regional-level training for participants from
multiple countries.
• Country training workshop: National and subnational training workshop.
• Regional workshop/ meeting:  Non-training key event attended by
participants from the region e.g. NITAG regional meetings, FETP Direct ors’
meetings, etc.
• Country workshop/ meeting: Non-training workshops or meetings that may
include meetings with national stakeholders.
• Field outreach:  activities that include field work and reach out such as
awareness campaigns, vaccination campaigns, engagements and meetings
with local communities, field visits to health centers, community centers, FETP
fieldwork, etc.
• Assessment/ Field Study : the even t pertains to conducting an assessment

GHD|EMPHNET’s Executive Director has the authority to approve and sign this
manual according to the endorsed authority matrix. The  Organizational Development
has the responsibility of reviewing the manual and ensuring its consistency with
internal policies and procedures and in compliance with best practices and internal
controls. The involved parties (Technical Team including the Operations team, Project
Management Office, Media and Communication, Information Technology Team)  in
this manual have the responsibility to review and keep this manual updated based on
the adopted manuals review procedures and authority matrix.
The Organizational Development and Quality Management are responsible of
performing regular reviews and monitoring to identify possible risks and to guarantee
that all measures are taken to prevent breaching of policies and/or procedures.
Global Health Development|Eastern Mediterranean Public Health Network (GHD|EMPHNET)
GHD|EMPHNET has the right to amend the policies mentioned in this manual  at any
time. Failure to comply with any of the policies will be considered actionable behavior
by senior management and could result  in disciplinary action up to and including
suspension or termination.
Purpose of the Manual
This manual aims to provides GHD|EMPHNET staff with the policies and procedures
to assure  systematic and standardized implementation of events with clear
responsibilities and authorities within a specific timeline.  The manual will ultimately
minimize concerns and problems as it is based on GHD|EMPHNET’s experience in
running events over the years.

[Section 01: PLANNING AND PREPARATION FOR THE EVENTS]
1.1. Purpose
This section aims  to set the policies, procedures, and guidelines for planning and
preparation phase for events conducted by GHD|EMPHNET.
1.2. Scope
Planning for an event is essential for assuring successful results. It requires team
effort, multitask management, communication, coordination, and collaboration.
Planning helps in implementing successful actions and in making decisions that can
prevent failure or mistakes. This section  presents the major areas that need to be
considered when planning an event. These topics are not inclusive as it is impossible
to plan for any unforeseen occurrence which are bound to occur even with the best
plans. The covered topics are standard issues that need to be considered when
planning an event to take place in regular and steady circumstances.  This section
applies to all personnel involved in planning and preparation phase.
1.3. Responsibilities
- It is the responsibility of  the Task Owner to initiate the process for the event,
and to provide the required information to the involved stakeholders to assure
timely and proper preparation for the event.
- When the event is conduct outside Jordan, it is the responsibility of the Task
Owner to make the required arrangements with t he representative in the
country.
- It is the responsibility of the Operations Officer to arrange for all required
logistics to prepare for the event on timely manner and according to the event
requirements and the policies mentioned in this section
- It is the responsibility of the relevant employee from Project Management Office
to monitor the implementation of the event according to the Gantt Chart and the
event plan.
- It is the responsibility of the Media and Communication Team to make all the
required arrangements according to the Task Owner’s request.
- It is the responsibility of the Finance Department to make sure that the event

[Section 01: PLANNING AND PREPARATION FOR THE EVENTS | Planning]
Advanced planning of events  is crucial for successful implementation. All
GHD|EMPHNET events are planned a head of time in order to secure ample time for
preparation. When organizing events, it is important to keep in mind the timeframe and
entailed costs.  Once the exact dates of the event are formally set in coordination
between Technical and Project Management teams, the Task Owner shall initiate
Event Request Process on the system at least one month before the event start date.
(Note: Sometimes the exact dates are not agreed upon till closer to the event. In this
case, the event can be initiated and start preparations while waiting for the
determination of the dates.)
Before starting the process on the system, the Task Owner  shall ensure proper
planning, acquire needed approvals, and collection of the required data to initiate the
process. At this stage, and to make sure of appropriate planning, our representatives
in the countries could be consulted whenever the need arises.  The Task Owner shall
be are aware that the below data provide the road map for the preparation and conduct
of the event and they will function as the guidelines and instructions for the different
departments. It is important to be aware that not all these field are considered required
for all events, this depends on the event nature, requirement and complexity.

Participants
Participant Identification process shall start four weeks before the event through
participants nomination/ invitation or registration:
1. Participants Nomination
In the case where the target audience names/ titles are not specified, i t is
necessary to prepare a letter to  target countries/ organizations  to ask for
nominations as soon as the event is scheduled. The Task Owner shall specify such
need and share the nomination list with the Operations Officer.
The letter shall list the event details and to request to share the names, titles and
contact information for the nominated candidates.
2. Participants Invitation
When participants titles or names  are identified, then invitation letters shall be
shared with their entities or directly to the participants sharing the related event
details and request participants to confirm their attendance.
Both nomination letters and invitation letters shall be prepared by the Task Owner,
reviewed by the Team Leader/ Director and signed by the Executive Director.  Once
the letter is approved from the technical team, the Operations Officer shall provide the
required coordination with the Administrative Team till the issuance of the letter
applying the approved policies and procedures for official letters issuance as per
Administrative Affairs Policies & Procedures Manual (ML-ADM-01).
Letters shall be shared thr ough the Admin istrative email keeping the Task Owner,
Team Leader/ Director, Country Focal Point and Operations Officer in the cc to follow
up receiving the response. In this email, the Country Focal Point or the Task Owner
shall be mentioned as a reference in case of any enquiries.

- Events venue could be at the premises of the trainees such as Ministries, or at

should be specified in the planning phase.
- If the training is at the premises of the target entities in the countries, The

- If there is a need to rent a venue, the Operations Officer or our representative

o Estimated number of participants (including facilitators  and any other

o Estimated number of rooms for accommodating participants and facilitators,

any.
o Need for special arrangements, such as head table, podium, flip charts, etc.
o Needed equipment, such as computer, projector, s ound system,
microphones, wireless connection, IT technical support, etc. If not provided
by the venue, a sound system organization shall be outsourced.
o Food and beverages required for the event.
Note: The cost of renting meeting rooms is often waived by hotels when
catering (lunch and coffee breaks) is offered for charge. Therefore, make
sure to include the catering services needed during the meeting/s.
o Other relevant information required for event conduct.
- Once the quotations  are received, they shall be analyzed by the Operations

o Availability of spacious meeting rooms (enough space to move around

Passports
- For external flights, valid passports shall be availa ble for the concerned
person(s).
- The Operations team shall check GHD|EMPHNET data base for the availability
of valid passports copies before contacting the concerned persons. Valid
passport should have validity of at least six months of the travel date.
- If a passport copy is available in our database; share an email with the
concerned person(s)  to confirm that the available copy is the latest vali d
passport, and he/she confirms to use it.
- If no passport copy is available in our database,  then the Operations Officer
shall contact the concerned person(s) requesting them to share it.
- Passports copies shall be kept in DMS T wenty, under the administration
channel, in the Passports folder under the relevant country.
- Passport copies shall be saved with the first and last name of the concerned
person.
- If passport copies in the database are outdated, they must be updated/replaced
by new copies within the same record.
Visa Issuances
The need for visa issuance for p articipants, facilitator or GHD|EMPHNET staff
shall be identified at early stage because in some cases it might take longer
than three weeks to obtain a visa. This shall be done by the Operations Officer
usually in coordination with the Task Owner.
- To ensure that the Operations Officer has the correct and valid information in
order to proceed with visa issuance and travel booking, a form (Annex 03) shall
be shared with participants and facilitators requesting them to fill the required
information. Form content could be updated based on the requirements.
The following scenarios for visa issuance could take place:
- Some countries request visitors to present a letter from GHD|EMPHNET to
verify their attendance at an event. In such cases, GHD|EMPHNET Operations
Officer issues visa support letters to participants (or facilitators) attending the
Global Health Development|Eastern Mediterranean Public Health Network (GHD|EMPHNET)

Officer issues visa support letters to participants (or facilitators) attending the
Global Health Development|Eastern Mediterranean Public Health Network (GHD|EMPHNET)
event, at least 2 weeks prior to the event. The information below should be
included in these letters:
o Full name (as it appears on participant’s passport)
o GHD|EMPHNET’s full name, title , and dates of the event that the
participant intends to attend.
o Include a fax number or email address for any information request
- For events conducted in Jordan and for those participants and facilitators who
come from countries where there is no Jordan embassy, GHD|EMPHNET
needs to support these by facilitating issuing their visas from Jordan’s
government.
The Operations Officer prepares the visa letters, signed by the Executive
Director and submit it to Ministry of Interior (MoI). Follow up with the MoI should
be through the focal point in coordination with the Operations Officer.
- For events conducted outside Jordan, the Operations Officer shall make the
required arrangements for visa issuance. However, i n certain c ases, visa
issuance could be supported by our representative in the country, while the
Operations Officer holds the responsibility of follow up and tracking.

- The Task Owner is responsible for preparing the event’s agenda in accordance

text:
[Section 02: Event Implementation]
2.1. Purpose
The purpose of this section is to set the policies, procedure, and guidelines for the
activities that shall take place before launching the event and during the event.
2.2. Scope
Conducting a successful event, required team effort, multitask management, and
effective communication. It is also required good skills for problem solving to face any
challenges during the event. The following topics are standard issues that need to be
considered when  conducting an event to take place in regular and steady
circumstances. This policy applies to all personnel involved in running the event.
2.3. Responsibilities
- It is the responsibility of the Operations Officer or the representative in the
country (who is responsible to logistical support) to be available during the
entire event to assure proper implementation of the planned items.
- It is the responsibility of the Logistics Officer to provide the required support to
the Operations Officer prior, during, and after the event  (This is mainly inside
Jordan).
- It is the responsibility of the Task Owner to ensure the event according to the
agenda and the plan.  Based on the event, the Task Owner shall attend the
event or coordinate with the Technical representative in the country to attend.
2.4. Policies:

metadata.document_title: Events Management Policies and Procedures Manual
metadata.section_path: S02: Event Implementation

text:
[Section 02: Event Implementation | Before Launching the event]
- To assure smooth implementation, every effort shall be made before the event
to make sure that all the required arrangements are made to achieve the
requirements that was requested in the planning phase.  Each team member
plays a crucial role in making the success of the event as follows.
- Event Site check shall be performed by the assigned team one day before the
event to make sure that the set up matches the requirements and to give time
to rectify any incident(s).
- In addition, the relevant team shall be one hour and half before the event start
time on the first day to reassure proper arrangements.
- The involved team in these preparations are usually the Operations Officer,
Logistics Officer, IT Specialist, plus a technical officer. However, based on the
circumstances and event location and country these functions could be
delegated to the representative in the country or other personnel. However, this
shall be monitored by the Operations Officer.
Global Health Development|Eastern Mediterranean Public Health Network (GHD|EMPHNET)

metadata.document_title: Events Management Policies and Procedures Manual
metadata.section_path: S02: Event Implementation > Before Launching the event

text:
[Section 02: Event Implementation | During the Event]
- The Operations Officer or the representative in the country and the Logistics
Officer should be always physically present during the event. They shall arrive
one hour before starting the daily program (other than the first day) to make the
required arrangements and should be the last one to leave the premises.
- The Operations Officer could request support from  the Logistics Officer in
accomplishing any task or arrangements, however, the Operations Officer
holds the ultimate responsibility.
- The Task Owner and/ or the Technical Team at the country should arrive to the
event site at least one hour prior to the start time to make sure  that all the
required arrangements are in place.
- Media and Communication team member(s) should attend the opening session
of the event and take appropriate notes and/ or photos.
- The Creative Lead shall make sure that the venue setup and all arrangements
are as planned.

metadata.document_title: Events Management Policies and Procedures Manual
metadata.section_path: S02: Event Implementation > During the Event

text:
[Section 02: Event Implementation | Delivering Payments to Participants and Facilitators]
- The Operations Officer shall coordinate delivering the payment with the
accounting department.
- In the case that participants  and facilitators attending events are entitled to a
per diem covering their period of stay. The Treasury Accountant or a delegate
is responsible for preparing and delivering these per diems.
- Delivering the per diem shall be on the second day of the event  for the events
that for more than one day. The Treasury Accountant or a delegate shall make
sure to distribute the per diem in a suitable time that doesn’t disturb the event
itself or the participants/ facilitators.
- When the event is conducted outside Jordan, the Treasury Accountant  shall
make the required coordination with the assigned person who will deliver the
payment to participants.
- Accounting policies and procedures shall be applied.

text:
[Section 02: Event Implementation | Social Program]
- It is not customary for GHD|EMPHNET to offer social activities or a social
program during the event. However, GHD|EMPHNET’s Operations Officer  or
the country representative is responsible for arranging trips or providing
information to any of the participants who wish to do sightseeing. Sometimes,
the participants wish to engage in a group dinner that is self -paid. In such
instances, the Operations Officer is responsible for making dinner reservations
for the group. Other times, GHD|EMPHNET Executive Office decides to invite
some of the participants or facilitators to a farewell and recognition dinner, for
which the Operations Officer will arrange reservations and inform the
concerned parties of details.

[Section 03: Closing the event]
3.1. Purpose
The purpose of this section is to set the policies, procedure, and guidelines for the
activities that shall take place upon event closure.
3.2. Scope
All events come to a conclusion and certain actions are required to wrap an event in
order to assure documentation of outcomes and achievements. Concluding an event
is not a sudden and rapid action as several issues need to be considered. This section
summarizes the issues need to be considered to  assure proper and efficient closing
of events. This policy applies to all personnel involved in event conduct closeout.
3.3. Responsibilities
It is the responsibility of the Task Owner and the Operations Officer to assure proper
close out of the event.
3.4. Policies

[Section 03: Closing the event | Payments]
The Operations Officer needs to present receipts retained from conducting the event
to the Finance Department together. The Treasury Accountant is responsible for
finalizing payment to the hotel or event site. S/he is responsible for cross-checking the
final guest list received from the hotel with the list provided by the Operations Officer.
The Treasury Accountant and any employee who received invoices shall submit them
to the Accounting team which by their turn will check them and upload them to the
system. After that the Finance Team shall record them to the relevant activity and
issue any required reports.

text:
[Section 03: Closing the event | Reporting]
Upon completing the event, the Task Owner is responsible for conducting a close-out
meeting with all relevant staff who were engaged in managing the event. The purpose
of this meeting is to discuss the event to identify and discuss any gaps or limitations
faced during the workshop. These meetings will help in identifying lessons learnt.
The Task Owner is responsible for preparing a report summarizing the event
proceedings (Technical report). This report should be prepared using GHD|EMPHNET
report template and should be presented for the Team Leader/ Director  within two
weeks from concluding the event through the system. Once reviewed and approved,
the report should be saved in its relevant folder on the DMS Twenty. The Task Owner
is also responsible for saving the material used during the event.
Documents Keeping
The Operations Officer is responsible for event documentation on the following sites:
- DMS Twenty/ Administration/ Project Tracking , by creating a new item
detailing the event details. This tracking is used for report generation and
projects tracking.
- Project Center/ Project Activity, by creating a new folder and nam e it
according to the event name, adding the final documents related to  the event
such as actual participants list, agenda, training material, and technical report.
- EMPHNET Resources Engine  (ERE), this site aims to collect data for all
participants who were involved in any of GHD|EMPHNET activities  (including
the past events). After each event, any new participants shall be added to the
ERE.
- Additional Consideration: It is extremely important to maintain accurate records
of participants in the EMPHNET Resources Engine (ERE) when collecting data
for participants of any event as they may also be involved in similar past
events/activities. After each event, any new participants shall be added to the
ERE. However, extreme caution must be practiced not to add duplicates to the

dedicated to serve the region by supporting national efforts to promote public health policies,
strategic planning, sustainable financing, resource mobilization, public health programs, and
other related services.

INTRODUCTION
This manual was prepared after thorough examination of available and accessible
policies and procedures. An extensive and thoroughly search was done in preparation
for this manual, which resulted in a comprehensive list of policies considered to be
applicable to the Gl obal health Development|  Eastern Mediterranean Public Health
Network (GHD|EMPHNET). MAUS Business Systems was used in drafting some of
the policies and procedures included in this manual. GHD|EMPHNET is responsible
for the results of the actions taken in accordance with the information provided in this
manual.
PURPOSE OF THE MANUAL
The Human Resources Policies and Procedures Manual (HR PPM) is a tool that was
created to facilitate the implementation of HR and personnel related systems and
functions. This PPM defines the primary HR related policies, rules and procedures
designed for, and adopted by, GHD|EMPHNET. Additionally, it defines the necessary
steps to be followed by the Human Resources Department and other concerned
parties for particular situations and also serves in identifying responsibilities, methods,
and means of executin g each step -in terms of communication channels, forms and
documents.

the Jordanian Labor Law and its amendments. All GHD|EMPHNET employees work

[Section 01: RECRUITMENT & SELECTION]
The Management of GHD|EMPHNET aims to develop and implement sufficient
Human Resources systems and procedures that support the achievement of
GHD|EMPHNET goals and objectives through implementing several HR programs
and processes.
In that regard and stemming from GHD|EMPHNET's interest in developing a system
that ensures the employment of highly qualified employees covering both external and
internal sources and means, for all levels at GHD|EMPHNET, A long with other
relevant HR systems and practices, the recruitment and selection syst em shall serve
in minimizing the turnover rate and assist in hiring the right people in the right positions.
Recruiting and selecting the right people is of paramount importance to the continued
success of GHD|EMPHNET. The recruitment and selection Policy set out how to
ensure, as far as possible, that the best people are recruited on merit and that the
recruitment process is free from bias and discrimination.
The recruitment and selection process encompasses three main stages, which are:
 Recruitment stage: starting from the vacancy occurrence and ending by issuing
shortlisted candidates to be interviewed.
 Selection stage: to interview shortlisted candidates and get a best applicant
available who meets all the selection criteria.
 Appointment stage: starting from choosing a candidate to fill the vacancy until the
end of the probationary period.
The recruitment and selection system includes a group of procedures for implementing
the above stages in a manner that ensures meeting employment needs and
requirements.

metadata.section_path: S01: RECRUITMENT & SELECTION

text:
[Section 01: RECRUITMENT & SELECTION | 1.1 Purpose]
The purpose of Recruitment and Selection system is to provide a framework and core
principles for recruitment and selection, in line with relevant legislation and equal
opportunities best practice, to ensure that the most suitable person is appointed and
merit-based selection is accomplished and different job requirements and objectives
are met.
In this context, GHD|EMPHNET embrace the following:
1 The System is based on an approach that customizes the R&S process as per
the requirements of th e different Managerial Levels which were identified in
the job description cards.
Global Health Development|Eastern Mediterranean Public Health Network (GHD|EMPHNET)
ML-HR-01, V.01  Page 19 of 158
2 The System favors and supports Internal Recruitment as a tool that facilitates
the attainment of optimal utilization of GHD|EMPHNET’s current human
capital, as well as increasing retentions rate.
3 The R&S System is mainly handled by the HR Department, which bears the
following advantages:
 Avoiding duplication of work and propagation of costs, since the HR
Department has a full oversight on the entire process.
 Increased effectiveness of the R&S process, especially as the process
matures in GHD|EMPHNET, since most teams have considerable yet
similar manpower requirements; it is advantageous to have the
recruitment process mainly handled by one designated entity.
 Enabling internal recruitment and thus an effective reallocation of
manpower.

[Section 01: RECRUITMENT & SELECTION | 1.2 Scope]
The Recruitment and Selection system is applicable to all vacant positions at
GHD|EMPHNET. Commencing from the development of the Human Resources Plan
and requesting to fill a vacancy until the end of the probationary period and converting

the right time. GHD|EMPHNET recruitment and selection system aims to ensure
attracting and appointing applicants with the right skills, knowledge, behaviors and
experience to meet the needs of all our vacancies. In light of this we ensure that
we appoint on the basis of merit and without discrimination
2. GHD|EMPHNET represented by the HR Department, is committed to ensure that
all Candidates are given equal access to information about the job vacancy and
its requirements, Candidates are considered on merit, Interviews and the selection
process are applied equally and consistently to candidates, and Selection
methods are reliable and free from bias or discrimination.

appoint the most qualified and competent candidates, and thus:

means and the most suitable sources

required process checks, where all candidates shall be treated equally
regardless of the source of recommendation

competencies

selection process unless meeting the minimum requirements of each phase

throughout the different phases of the R&S process in case they possess

information shall be treated in strict confidence, and access to such shall be

[Section 02: PERFORMANCE APPRAISAL | 2.1 Purpose]
The purpose of the Performance Appraisal (PA) system is to offer a fair and balanced
review and appraisal of GHD|EMPHNET employee’s performance during their
contract period.

metadata.section_path: S02: PERFORMANCE APPRAISAL > 2.1 Purpose

text:
[Section 02: PERFORMANCE APPRAISAL | 2.2 Scope]
The Performance Appraisal (PA) system is applied for all full-time employees at
GHD|EMPHNET.

metadata.section_path: S02: PERFORMANCE APPRAISAL > 2.2 Scope

text:
[Section 02: PERFORMANCE APPRAISAL | 2.3 Responsibilities]
The responsibility of implementing the PA falls upon the HR De partment, as well as
the employee’s direct manager and Concerned Director/ Team Leader. The reason
behind this joint responsibility is to ensure that the process is being performed
according to the approved procedures via formal interaction with each appraiser.

metadata.section_path: S02: PERFORMANCE APPRAISAL > 2.3 Responsibilities

text:
[Section 02: PERFORMANCE APPRAISAL | 2.4 Policies]
1. The employee performance appraisal seeks to achieve the following:
 Giving the employee and the direct manager the opportunity to set the
employee goals’ and expected accomplishments during the contract period.
 Reviewing employee performance  effectively in an objective and fair
manner.
 Identifying employees' concealed potentials to ascertain the possibility of
adding more responsibilities or recommending transfer to a more
challenging position.
 Identifying weaknesses in performance and ensuri ng their treatment
through employee development forming a key input to training needs
assessment.
 Detecting mismatches between job -holders and their positions, hence
assisting in improving the recruitment and selection process.
 Increasing motivation and sa tisfaction levels among employees, thus
boosting morale which has positive impact on quality of work and
productivity.
2. The employee performance appraisal should be carried out Annually; through
initiating the process on the Mena-Me HR system. While performance review will
be carried out semiannually.
3. Human Resources shall initiate the process of performance review in the middle
of contract, this evaluation is considered as a middle evaluation to make sure that
employee’s performance effectively archives the preset objectives. In addition, it
gives an opportunity for both the Direct Manager and employees to share any
comments, recommendations, requirements and challenges. Objectives could be
updated accordingly.
Global Health Development|Eastern Mediterranean Public Health Network (GHD|EMPHNET)
ML-HR-01, V.01  Page 53 of 158
4. The employees are evaluated based on their performance related to their duties,
responsibilities, competencies, behavior, and relations with other employees.
5. The direct manager should be aware of the employee performance during the
performance appraisal period in terms of his/ her duties and responsibi lities.
[Part 1 of 4 — more points continue in related chunks]

metadata.section_path: S02: PERFORMANCE APPRAISAL > 2.4 Policies

text:

5. The direct manager should be aware of the employee performance during the
performance appraisal period in terms of his/ her duties and responsibi lities.
6. In case the employee has more than one Direct Manager during the appraisal
period, then all concerned managers should participate in the employee
performance appraisal  if the  working period under each Direct manager is
reasonable (3 months and above).
7. The performance appraisal should take into consideration the whole performance
appraisal period not only part of it, and it should focus on the performance and
accomplishments.
8. The PA will be officially applied for all new employees who join GHD|EMPHN ET
5 months prior to the launching to the Performance Appraisal.
9. When setting the performance goals, both the employee and his /her Direct
Manager should ensure that the goals are SMART:
 Specific: the goal should be clearly defined.
 Measurable: the goal is measurable so that direct manager has tangible
evidence that the employee met/ partially met/ not met the goal
 Achievable: humanly possible and has all the required resources.
 Realistic: within the availability of resources, knowledge and time. Also;
relevant to the employee's role, skills and qualifications
 Time bounded: set deadlines and enough time to achieve the desired goal.
10. The set goals of each employee will be evaluated based on three rating
descriptors:
 Met the goal (100%)
 Partially met the goal (1%-99%)
 Not met the goal (0%)
11. Employee performance during the appraisal period will be evaluated based on 4
main criteria each is divided into sub criterion, the elements and their weights will
be based on the employee level/ position:
 Soft Skills (6 elements)
• Reliability/ Accountability
• Civility and respect
• Communication Skills
• Relationship with co-workers
• Taking Initiative
• Teamwork

12. Employee performance during the appraisal period will be evaluated based
on five rating descriptors:
 Outstanding (5): Performance far exceeded expectations due to
exceptionally high quality of work performed in all essential areas of
responsibility, resulting in an overall quality of work that was superior.
 Meets Expectations (4): Performance consistently meet expectations in
all essential areas of responsibility, and the quality of work overall was
excellent.
 Somehow below Expectations (3): Performance consistently do meet
minimum standards of acceptability in all essential areas of responsibility
 Improvement Needed (2): Performance did not consistently meet
expectations – performance failed to meet expectations in one or more
essential areas of responsibility.  A professional development plan to
improve performance must be set
 Unsatisfactory (1): Performance was consistently below expectations in
most essential areas of responsibility. Significant improvement is needed
in one or more important areas. A plan to correct performance must be
set.
13. The Direct Manager should consider facts in the performance appraisal and
conduct it in a fair and objective manner.

[Section 03: EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT | 3.1 Purpose]
To provide instructions and steps needed to renew/end employment of a contracted
employee with GHD|EMPHNET according to the conditions of employment specified
in the contract. As well as to standardize the process of accepting/rejecting employees’
resignations while ensuring that all work requirements are met, all relevant documents
completed, and entitlements paid, in order to make sure that all employees are treated
in accordance with Jordanian Labor Law and the HR Policies and Procedure Manual.

metadata.section_path: S03: EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT > 3.1 Purpose

text:
[Section 03: EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT | 3.2 Scope]
This section is applicable on all current employees who have an employment contract
with GHD|EMPHNET, whether their contracts will be renewed/ terminated, or they are
not welling to continue/ renew their employment with GHD|EMPHNET.

metadata.section_path: S03: EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT > 3.2 Scope

text:
[Section 03: EMPLOYMENT CONTRACT | 3.3 Responsibilities]
It is the primary responsibility of the Human Resource Department to coordinate and
implement the processes of employees’ contract renewal, ending, and resignation.
- To coordinate between the dismissed employee and all other Departments to
ensure a smooth and professional exit process.
- To ensure the overall completion of the resignation in coordination with the
concerned Teams/Departments as well as a smooth handover is taking place
during the notice period.
- To coordinate between the employee, Direct Manager, and the Team
Leader/Director to ensure a smooth and professional contract renewal
process.

-Upon contract end for any reason, the Direct Manager shall determine the faith of
the employee email, whether to be deactivated, sharing the emails back up with any
employee, keep the email active and to be assigned to the Direct Manager or to one
of the team.

be re-evaluated after three months with the Direct Manager.
- Upon exit interview, the employee shall be informed politely to exit the WhatsApp

- HR team shall notify GHD|EMPHNET employees upon employees resignation one
week prior the end date, and to specify the new point of contact.
- Employees are requested to bring social security status upon contracts renewal.

[Section 04: TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT | 4.1 Purpose]
The Training and Development system aims to develop and implement sufficient
Human Resources systems and procedures that support the achievement of
GHD|EMPHNET goals and objectives through implementing several HR programs
and processes, ensure that all employees receive sufficient training that contributes to
developing their skills and enhancing their daily job performance, and assess and
identify the existing Competency gaps and the training needs on the individual,
functional and organizational levels.

metadata.section_path: S04: TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT > 4.1 Purpose

text:
[Section 04: TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT | 4.2 Scope]
The Training and Development System outlines the process of identifying, estimating,
prioritizing training needs and developing training plans that are applicable to all the
employees at GHD|EMPHNET. It also defines the procedures and criteria of
suggesting, requesting, and evaluating training.

metadata.section_path: S04: TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT > 4.2 Scope

text:
[Section 04: TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT | 4.3 Responsibilities]
1. It is the responsibility of the HR Team in cooperation with Directors/Team
Leaders to develop and update a consistent Annual Training Plan.
2. It is the responsibility of the HR Team in c ooperation with Directors/Team
Leaders to assess and prioritize training needs.
3. It is the responsibility of the HR Team in cooperation with all GHD|EMPHNET’s
concerned Directors, Direct Managers, and Employees to request a training
outside approved training plan.
4. It is the responsibility of the HR Team in cooperation with all GHD|EMPHNET’s
concerned Direct Managers/Team Leader and Employees to evaluate the
effectiveness and benefit of a specific training activity and its compliance to the
Organization’s objectives and policies.

metadata.section_path: S04: TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT > 4.3 Responsibilities

text:
[Section 04: TRAINING AND DEVELOPMENT | 4.4 Policies]
1. The training and development system should include a group of procedures for
implementing training in a manner that ensures meeting training needs and
adapting to technological and organizational changes.
Global Health Development|Eastern Mediterranean Public Health Network (GHD|EMPHNET)
ML-HR-01, V.01  Page 77 of 158
2. The training and development system should ensure that all employees receive
sufficient training that contributes to developing their skills and enhancing their
daily job performance, thus, enabling them to carry out their duties safely and
without risk to themselves or others.
3. GHD|EMPHNET is committed to align training activities with its goals and
strategic plans and direct it towards supporting individual and organizational
performance and provide an effective liaison with local and international training
Vendor organizations.
4. GHD|EMPHNET is committed to distribute training resources equally among
employees to ensure progress and professional growth of all employees and
internal equity among employees in their training opportunities.
5. GHD|EMPHNET shall allocate an annu al training budget as part of the
organization identified budget.
6. GHD|EMPHNET staff who is eligible for training and development must have
worked for GHD|EMPHNET for a minimum of nine months before they qualify
for any training, unless the training is dedi cated to new employees or a
prerequisite for job performance, such as technical training. In this case, the
trainee shall be provided with a complete training course schedule.
7. A training report must be submitted within 2 weeks from the date the employee
completes a training course. Employees will not be recommended for another
training course unless their report for the previous course was submitted in a
timely manner and within acceptable standards.
8. Employees who completed a training course and in coordina tion with their

 Development Stage: in this stage, training needs are assessed on the
organizational, occupational  and individual levels. In addition, training
objectives are determined, vendors are selected, and training plans are
developed in this stage.
 Implementation Stage : this stage includes the selection of training
contents and the implementation of training c ourses that meet the
identified training needs.
 Evaluation Stage: in this stage, certain criteria are used to determine if
the training has achieved the desired objectives.

[Section 05: ATTENDANCE, LEAVES & VACATIONS | 5.1 Purpose]
To provide a system within GHD|EMPHNET for monitoring and controlling employee
vacations, leaves, regular attendance, and punctuality in a manner which ensures
the sustainability of work activities and accomplishments.

metadata.section_path: S05: ATTENDANCE, LEAVES & VACATIONS > 5.1 Purpose

text:
[Section 05: ATTENDANCE, LEAVES & VACATIONS | 5.2 Scope]
This procedure applies to all full-time employees at GHD|EMPHNET.

text:
[Section 05: ATTENDANCE, LEAVES & VACATIONS | 5.3 Responsibilities]
1. It is the responsibility of Human Resources team to monitor employees’ working
hours, analyze and manage employees’ monthly attendance sheet  and to
propose solutions to any attendance issues.
2. The HR Manager is responsible for sending a monthly Employee Attendance
Logs to the Financial & Admin Affairs Director at GHD|EMPHNET, as per the
current HR-adopted system.
3. Managers are responsible for mo nitoring the daily attendance of their team
members.
4. Managers are responsible for informing the HR team by email of employee
absences.
5. GHD|EMPHNET employees are responsible for recording their actual times of
departure and return of business and personal leaves using the Mena HR
system and the attendees scanner.
6. The HR team is responsible for the implementation of all relevant policies and
procedure.
7. Direct managers are responsible for the preparation and planning of their team
members’ annual vacations in  a manner which sustains the levels of
productivity and tasks achievement. This includes the decision to obtain and
assign a substitute for the vacationing employee if necessary.
8. The HR Department is responsible for studying annual vacation plans and
ensuring their consistency with due dates and vacation balances.
9. The human resources team in consultation and coordination with the respective
team leader, should be responsible for implementing working from anywhere
policy and for ensuring commitment and adherence.
10. It is the direct manager’s responsibility to ensure that work commitments are
provided for when considering the personal needs of each employee's leave
request. Managers must consider providing a substitute employee to handle
the duties and responsi bilities of the vacationing employee to ensure that
his/her absence does not cause work dissatisfaction whilst also avoiding the
accumulation of outstanding leave.

[Section 05: ATTENDANCE, LEAVES & VACATIONS | 5.4 Policies | Employee Attendance]
1. Working hours for GHD|EMPHNET employees must not exceed 48 hours per
week with a maximum of 10 hours per day. During the month of Ramadan, the
actual working hours shall be reduced to a maximum of six hours a day or thirty-
six hours per week.
2. Each employee of GHD|EMPHNET must have at least one day of rest per
week. For GHD|EMPHNET, this day is Friday. Though Saturdays are usually
non-working days, occasionally employees may be requested to work on
Saturday as deemed necessary according to the load of work. Should this be
the case, management will notify the employee(s) who are requested to work
on a specific Saturday and the employee(s) must comply accordingly without
requesting any compensation.
3. GHD|EMPHNET follows the official holidays announced by the Jordanian
Government.
4. GHD|EMPHNET employees shall use the specified entrances and exits and
shall arrive and leave work at the defined times that are communicated to them
including daily arrival and departure times and scheduled shift times (if
applicable).
5. All GHD|EMPHNET employees shall use the attendance scanner located at
GHD|EMPHNET’s entrances to record the times of their arriving and departing
the work premises.
6. The daily working hours of GHD|EMPHNET employees shall not be less than
8 hours a day, including the lunch break.
a. Flexible working hours are from 8:30 a.m. – 5:30 p.m. each employee
has to attend at least 8 hours daily between these hours to accumulate
8 hours of attendance on every working day. However, the working hours
for Financial & Administrative Affairs is for 08:30 a.m. – 05:00 p.m.
7. GHD|EMPHNET employees should arrive to work before 9:30 a.m. and shall
not leave work before 4:30 p.m.
8. Regular late check-ins after 9:30 a.m. and/or early check-outs before 4:30 p.m.
are considered a violation of the attendance policy and will be handled in

text:
[Section 05: ATTENDANCE, LEAVES & VACATIONS | 5.4 Policies | Personal Leave and Annual Vacations]
1. All GHD|EMPHNET permanent employees, after probation period, are entitled
a total of 10 hours of personal leave per month or three weeks (15 working
days) paid annual leave accrued on a pro-rata basis, and employees much take
their annual leave “vacation” during the contract period.
2. Personal leave should be limited to the minimum time required to complete the
personal job. Personal leave should not exceed 3 hours each time and should
not be less than 30 minutes each time.
3. If a ny of the personal leaves exceeds 3 hours, then a one -day vacation (8
hours) shall be deducted from the concerned employee annual vacation
balance.
4. Accumulating eight hours of personal leave time will be considered the same
as a one -day vacation (8 hours) and will be deducted from the concerned
employee’s annual vacation balance.
5. If an employee exceeded amount of time of late check -ins and/or personal
leaves has also depleted the employee’s annual vacation balance, the
exceeded time shall then be deducted from the employee’s salary.
6. Prior to the actual time of taking a personal leave, an employee must first take
permission from his/her direct manager and must apply and request the leave
on the Mena-Me HR System.
7. If a direct manager denies approval of person al leave requests, they shall
communicate a reasonable cause for denying the request to the concerned
employee.
8. A GHD|EMPHNET employee shall not leave the office before obtaining the
approval of his/her direct manager except in cases of emergency.
9. The direct manager must ensure that employees are not abusing their right to
a personal leave.
10. GHD|EMPHNET employees are eligible for an annual vacation only after
completion of the probation period at GHD|EMPHNET; the employee shall refer
to his next level manager if he/she needs to take an annual vacation before the
end of the probation period.

[Section 05: ATTENDANCE, LEAVES & VACATIONS | 5.4 Policies | Working from Anywhere (WfA)]
1. WfA can be initiated by management or requested by empl oyee for specific
reasons.
2. Management may apply WfA, hybrid module, Working from Office to
employees/ teams based on health status and/ or work requirements.  Clear
instructions will be shared with employees regarding their working modules
3. Employees working from offices  whose nature of their work does not require
them to be at the office is eligible for 6 days per month to work from anywhere.
4. Employee whose nature of work requires them to be located in a country, other
than those assigned to work directly w ith ministries/stakeholders is eligible for
6 days per month.
5. The following positions are not eligible for WfA requests: Accounting Manager,
Senior Accountant, Accountant, Junior Accountant, Treasury Accountant,
Logistics Supervisor, Logistics Officer, Mai ntenance Officer, Driver, Office
Assistant and Receptionist.
6. The Executive Director, based on the recommendation of the HR Manager,
teams leaders and Directors, will approve any future amendments needed,
including the list of all positions who are eligible for working from anywhere.
7. The Human Resources should be informed of all employees who will be
working from anywhere.
8. When working from anywhere, both employee and his/her direct manager
should set boundaries on work schedule and adhere to the official  working
hours. The official working hours should not be less than 8 hours a day.
9. Working period is from 8:30 a.m. – 5:30 p.m. Eligible employees are expected
to be working 8 hours during this time and in agreement with their direct
manager.
10. All internal/Bi-weekly/one-on-one meetings should be scheduled to take place
during the organization’s core working hours (8:30 a.m. – 5:30 p.m.).
11. WfA employees should be accessible for using video conferencing with
Microsoft Teams or Zoom.

[Section 05: ATTENDANCE, LEAVES & VACATIONS | 5.4 Policies | Unpaid Vacation]
1. All Un-paid vacations are subject to the approval of the Executive Director.
2. GHD|EMPHNET could grant unpaid vacations for employees up to a maximum
of 20 days per year, under the following circumstances:
 If the employee exhausted all his/her annual vacation days.
 If t he type of the leave needed does not match any of the leave types
available at GHDEMPHNET.
 The reason of the leave should be acceptable to GHD|EMPHNET, all
concerned management and HR.
 The vacation leave does not conflict with job requirements and the normal
operations of GHD|EMPHNET.
3. In times of emergency when the vacation balance of the employee in need of
vacation is insufficient, the Executive Director is entitled, upon the
recommendation of the concerned manager, to grant the employee an
Global Health Development|Eastern Mediterranean Public Health Network (GHD|EMPHNET)
ML-HR-01, V.01  Page 94 of 158
emergency unpaid vacation, provided that the total vacation days taken do not
exceed 20 continuous or intermittent days. If an unpaid vacation exceeds the
permitted consecutive 20 days, the employment contract shall be deemed
suspended unless contractually agreed to otherwise.
4. Extending unpaid vacation (more than 20 days) is subject to the direct
manager recommendation and the Executive Director’s approval and based
on the job availability upon return or continuity of service.
5. In case of an emergency, the employee requesting a vacation shall be
provided with top priority to facilitate and complete all steps entailed in the
procedure in a timely and convenient manner.
6. In extraordinary and justifiable circumstances, leave without pay shall not be
granted:
 When an empl oyee has an entitlement to accrued or pro rata annual
leave
 When work commitments cannot be met during the proposed leave.
7. When leave without pay is granted, in most cases continuity of service will be

as the medical examination period shall be treated as si ck leave days and
accordingly deducted from the sick leave balance.

Labor Law and relevant acting Jordanian legislations.
7. If an employee becomes ill during vacation, the sick days will not be considered
a sick leave but will be deemed part of the employee’s annual vacation.

and occasions announced by of the Jordanian Government.

[Section 05: ATTENDANCE, LEAVES & VACATIONS | 5.4 Policies | Hajj Vacation]
1. Employees shall be entitled to a paid leave of 14 days to perform Hajj, granted
only once during an employee’s service.
2. To be eligible for this holiday, the employee must have spent at least 3
consecutive years with GHD|EMPHNET from their first contract date.
3. GHD|EMPHNET has the right to determine the number of workers who shall be
given this vacation annually in accordance with work requirements and taking
into consideration the number of years of the employee’s service at
GHD|EMPHNET.

[Section 05: ATTENDANCE, LEAVES & VACATIONS | 5.4 Policies | Emergency Vacation]
GHD|EMPHNET employees are entitled to the following emergency vacations that are
granted occasionally given that these do not exceed a total of six days spread over
one year for any of the following reasons and based on conditions imposed by
management. No two of the following case scenarios can be combine in the same
month, unless deemed appropriate by management:
1. Three days paid vacation because of marriage of employee.
Global Health Development|Eastern Mediterranean Public Health Network (GHD|EMPHNET)
ML-HR-01, V.01  Page 96 of 158
2. Three days paid vacation given to the employee in the case of the death of one
of the first or second relatives (husband or wife, a parent, a son or daughter, a
brother or sister, a grandfather or grandmother, father - or mother-in-law). One
day vacation for the death of employee’s direct aunt or uncle.
3. Three days paid vacation is given to female employees if she must accompany
her child to the hospital upon providing proof via a medical report.
4. In any one of the following cases, a one day paid vacation is given to an
employee:
a. Attendance of surgery for a blood-relative or next-of-kin family member
b. Admission of a parent, child, or spouse to the hospital as their caretaker
c. Death of an uncle, aunt, nephew, or niece
d. A serious traffic accident involving a parent, husband, wife, child, or
sibling.
5. Any emergency leave requests for a reason not mentioned herewith shall
depend on the Executive Director’s directive. Otherwise, and if not reported
over the telephone or the      Mena-Me HR system, absence with no reason will
be considered as absence without excuse. The penalty impose d will be taken
according to the sequence of penalties that will follow later, and the day will be
deducted from the employee annual vacation balance or salary of the employee
or will otherwise be kept at the discretion of management.

text:
[Section 05: ATTENDANCE, LEAVES & VACATIONS | 5.4 Policies | Maternity Leave]
Female employees are entitled to the following:
1. Ten weeks (70 days) of maternity leave with full pay before and after childbirth
provided that the period after the childbirth shall not be less than six weeks.
2. One-year full-time vacation without pay to raise her children. However, if she works
elsewhere during this period, she might lose her right to return to work.
3. A breastfeeding period to breastfeed her  newborn during working hours at full
payment for one year from the date of birth provided that this does not exceed one
hour per day.

annual leave, personal leave, or b usiness leave, and should submit the leave

2. Any vacation obtained without following the required procedure is deemed absence

[Section 06: DISCIPLINE, GRIEVANCE & COMPLAINTS | 6.1 Purpose]
The purpose of Discipline procedures is to ensure the commitment and adherence
of all GHD|EMPHNET employees to the internal regulations and policies of
GHD|EMPHNET. While the Grievance procedure provide a system for grievance
process that ensures employee equity and fairness because of an internal act that
is perceived as causing injustice, personal work obstruction or violating work
policies and procedures affecting the employee.  The complaint procedure aims to
provide fair, open and clear process  for complaints and ensure a satisfactory
outcome for all GHD|EMPHNET employees.

metadata.section_path: S06: DISCIPLINE, GRIEVANCE & COMPLAINTS > 6.1 Purpose

text:
[Section 06: DISCIPLINE, GRIEVANCE & COMPLAINTS | 6.2 Scope]
Discipline and Grievance are applicable to all prospective or current employees of
the GHD|EMPHNET. For the Discipline, the process starts when the Direct Manager
notices or is informed of a violation made by the employee till The HR Manager
formally notifies the employee of the violation that the employee committed in detail
and the disciplinary action taken against him/her. For the Grievance, the process
starts from submitting the grievance request until informing the employee of the
formal verdict of the grievance.  The complaint policy starts when the employee
submit a complaint request until informing the employee of the formal verdict of the
complaint.

metadata.section_path: S06: DISCIPLINE, GRIEVANCE & COMPLAINTS > 6.2 Scope

text:
[Section 06: DISCIPLINE, GRIEVANCE & COMPLAINTS | 6.3 Responsibilities]
1. It is the responsibility of the Human Resources team to periodically updating
employees with internal bylaw, policies and regulations in addition to any
disciplinary actions related to their violation
2. The Human Resources Manager is responsibl e for the supervision of the
implementation of the Discipline, Grievance & Complaint policies.
3. It is the responsibility of the HR Department in cooperation with all
GHD|EMPHNET’s concerned Manager/ Team Leader & Director and the
Grievance Committee to conduct the grievance process.
4. It is the responsibility of the Human Resources to handle the employees’
complaints and to determine the disciplinary action after a deep investigation in
all the aspect of complaints received from the employees.

[Section 06: DISCIPLINE, GRIEVANCE & COMPLAINTS | 6.4 Policies]
Discipline:
1. GHD|EMPHNET acts against employees who are proven to be responsible for
committing violations such as those mentioned in internal bylaw, violating any

any form of discip linary penalties, where a verbal or written notice or a first or

in addition to deducting late or absence penalties when they occur.
2. Employees shall be informed and continually updated with any new or updated
internal regulations and policies and the disciplinary actions related to their
violation.
3. The disciplinary actions applied at GHD|EMPHNET shall be in line with the ones
detailed in GHD|EMPHNET internal bylaw and in complia nce with the
Jordanian Labor Law.
4. All disciplinary actions are not valid after 15 days after revealing the violation
and taking no action to investigate it.
5. An employee committing more than one violation at the same time shall be
disciplined with the highe st disciplinary action of the consecutive committed
violations.
6. No more than one penalty is stated for each violation and no penalties are
added up.
7. Penalties are implemented only after informing the concerned employee about
the violation he/she committed and ensuring that he/she receives Violation
Notification of the related penalty he / she is subject to. If he / she refuses to
receive the document or sign it, two witnesses shall sign that the employee was
informed  but refused to sign about the penalties.
8. GHD|EMPHNET employees shall be granted the chance to defend their cases
prior to imposing the penalties and such defenses shall be documented in
writing.
9. GHD|EMPHNET may not conduct any penalties for violations committed

of the cause of grievance.
20. Any employee with a grievance who requests any document shall not be denied
access, provided that the document directly relates to the subject of the
grievance and the employee has the authority to review these documents.
21. The period extending from the date the employee submitted his grievance until
the date of informing him of the formal verdict shall not exceed 15 working days.
22. If an employee needs to file a grievance against his direct manager, then the
grievance is to be filed with the next level manager.
23. If the grievance is against the HR team member, the Human Resources
Manager is responsible for carrying out the requirements of this procedure.

Health Insurance
1. GHD|EMPHNET covers its employees who want to join the health insurance and
their family (Wife/ husband and children) through including them in one of the
insurance companies working in Jordan according to the approved insurance
policy, after successfully completing the probation period.
2. GHD|EMPHNET pays full membership for health insurance of its employees their
families (Wife/ husband and children) and shall not bear the cost of any medical,
surgical, or other services that are not included in the medical insurance plan.
3. All employees shall abide by all rules, conditions, terms, and restrictions mentioned
in the medical insurance policy available at GHD|EMPHNET.
4. Once a GHD|EMPHNET employee contract is ended , then the employee shall
return all the insurance related items to the human resources.
5. GHD|EMPHNET employees traveling on business assignments shall be  issued
travel medical insurance prior to the travel date unless it is required earlier for visa
issuance.
6. GHD|EMPHNET employees traveling on monthly basis and/or for long business
trips (more than five times a year) especially to certain countries shall have annual
travel medical insurance or as decided by GHD|EMPHNET.

Internal Communication Guideline
April 10th, 2023
GHD|EMPHNET: Working Together for Better Health
The Eastern Mediterranean Public Health Network (EMPHNET) is a regional network that
focuses on strengthening public health systems in the Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR)
and beyond. EMPHNET works in partnership with ministries of health, non -government
organizations, international agencies, private sector, and relevant institutions from the region
and the globe to promote public health and applied epidemiology. To advance the work of
EMPHNET, Global Health Development (GHD) was initiated to build coordination
mechanisms with partners and collaborators. Together, GHD|EMPHNET is dedicated to
serving the region by supporting efforts to promote public health policies, strategic planning,
sustainable financing, resource mobilization, public health programs, and other related areas.

Introduction
Communication is a two -way process that disseminates data and information.
Lasswell's Maxim defines communication as “who says what to whom in what
channel with what effect”. Communication is exchanging of information from one
point to the other point in an efficient manner.  Effective communication is the key

[Continued: this topic — Part 2 of 2]
channel with what effect”. Communication is exchanging of information from one
point to the other point in an efficient manner.  Effective communication is the key
to success in life, work, and relationships  as it minimizes misunderstandings,
errors, frustration, and conflic t. Effective communication is essential in enabling
GHD|EMPHNET to achieve its mission, values, and goals, improve its operation ,
and encourage decentralization within clear lines of command based on the
authority matrix.  Clear policies and guidelines  on communication standards will
standardize communication among all teams. The adherence to such policies will
enable effective and efficient communication  and enhance information flow , and
eventually improve delivering the organization’s mandate.
Building internal communications capacity means providing timely and effective
information to all staff, linking offices across the Organization, and enhancing
stronger employee engagement , and facilitating dialogue , discussion, and
information exchange.

[Purpose]
This document aims to build the  employees capacity on an effective
communication practice by providing them with general guidelines and
professional practices on internal communication. For this purpose, this document
covers more specific details on benefits of effective internal communication, main
principles of effective internal communication, and the steps required for effective
communication. It also highlights  the major obstacles in communication  and how
to overcome them through considering the importance of communications in
diverse work groups . It also shed the light on the  essential communication
channels which are broadly used at GHD|EMPHNET  and needed by the
employees to communicate with different parties  internally. Further more, this
document provides employees with the needed information to manage information
flow with stakeholders in a more efficient and effective manner.
This document targets all teams at HQ and Country Offices and, to some extent
with external parties . Additionally, it  describes the planned and periodic
communication occurring between different internal communication s platforms.
Hence, the ultimate purpose of this document is to guide the implementation of
GHD|EMPHNET opera tions, and it defines  information that needs to be
communicated between GHD|EMPHNET divisions, teams, and units.

text:
[Responsibility]
GHD|EMPHNET is committed to ensuring that appropriate policies, procedures , and
monitoring arrangements are in place to support good internal communications at HQ
and Country Offices. On the other hand, employees should communicate effectively
to enhance the productive working environment and ensure success in delivering
GHD|EMPHNET’s operational goals and plans.
Managers, Team Leaders, and Directors are responsible to ensure implementation of
effective communication within their team s and other teams . They should create an
open and informative culture where all employees are encouraged to seek and give
information.
Employees are responsible to follow the principles and steps of effective
communication, share information in a timely manner, and seek information that is
relevant to their work.
EMPHNET’s Executive Director has the responsibility to approve and sign this
guideline according to the endorsed authority matrix.
The Quality Management  team is responsible for performing regular reviews and
monitoring progress, in order  to identify possible risks and to guarantee that all
measures are taken to prevent the breaching of policies and/or procedures.
GHD|EMPHNET has the right to amend this guideline at any time. Failure to comply
with the policies or instructions mentioned in this document could result in disciplinary
action up to and including suspension or termination.

text:
[Section 01: Effective Communication | Benefits of Effective Internal Communication]
Effective internal communication between all internal participants i.e. employees,
management, or consultants , creates a cohesive culture where everyone is
focused on the same goals. By working within a cohesive culture, different teams
can work more efficiently, and they can collaborate more effectively. Some specific
benefits that can result from effective internal communication include:
• Internal Brand Awareness: to ensure that all employees are aware of the
organization’s mission and vision.
• Employee Engagement : to keep  all employees abreast with all
organizational updates, news, achievements, new projects, and
partnerships, etc.
• Enabling Change within the Organization: to enable and empower all
employees to make decisions themselves by having the tools and
knowledge they need to make decisions that are  in line with the
organization’s goals.
• Building a Culture of Open Communication: to provide a number of
channels and platforms for all teams to share useful resources and
information, to lessen duplication of work and to strengthen impact.
• Driving Organizational Performance: to reduce the day -to-day conflict
since conflicts usually are  the result of different opinions on  what is
important to the organization.
• Build an Organizational Culture: Where people work together effec tively
towards a common goal.

metadata.section_path: S01: Effective Communication > Benefits of Effective Internal Communication

text:
[Section 01: Effective Communication | Main Principles of Effective Internal Communication]
Ineffective internal  communication is usually either arbitrary or incomplete  or
planned only in reaction to specific events. However, E ffective internal
communication should be always planned, not only to deal with specific issues, but
for the well-being of the organization, in the long run.
In this document, some  basic principles need to be adopted to ensure effective
internal communication across the organization.
These include;
• Long-term focus
• Values to be clearly communicated.
• Communication strategy is crucial for successful and effective internal
communication.
• Consistency in spreading messages.
• Being proactive
• Creating and maintaining a positive image.
• Tailored to the audience (both in delivery and content)
• Communicating in timely manner
While communication and disseminating work related messages and information on a
timely basis is essential for work success, confidentiality and privacy aspects of some
data and information should be taken into consideration during the work dissemination.

metadata.section_path: S01: Effective Communication > Main Principles of Effective Internal Communication
metadata.policy_name: Main Principles of Effective Internal Communication

text:
[Section 01: Effective Communication | Identify Communication Requirements]
Employee should know what the requirements of successful communications are to
plan on how to achieve those requirements.  He/she should first identify who needs
what information. Stakeholders need different types of information, depending on their
interest and priority. Besides, it is essential to determine the channels of
communication, how often the information is needed , involved departments, the
number of individuals involved, etc.  and that there are no gaps in everyone's'
understanding.

metadata.section_path: S01: Effective Communication > Identify Communication Requirements

text:
[Section 01: Effective Communication | Identify the 5Ws (Why, What, When, Where, Who) and 1H (How)]
Identify the 5Ws (Why, What, When, Where, Who) and 1H (How) is one of the methods
that used to assist in identifying communication requirements as the following:
• Who needs to be communicated to.
• What needs to be communicated  taking into consideration the confidentiality
and privacy aspects.
• When it should be communicated, and the timeline of communication should
be monitored.
• Where should it be communicated. If the team involves many people, then
individual level and team level communications needs to be resolved.
• Why communication of information is essential and to what level is important.
• How the communication needs to be done; via e-mail, phone, etc.
Figure 1: The 5 “W's” and 1 “H”
Identify and Accommodate the Enterprise Environmental Factors and
Organizational Process Assets
Much of the day-day communication is linked to the enterprise environmental factors
and Organizational Process Assets. All employees should review and identify these
factors and assets to ensure effective communication. These includes:
• Organizational culture and structure,
• Standard, regulations, policies, and procedures,
• The logistics and the organizational infrastructure,
• The human resources,
• The authorization matrix,
• Information system.
• Workflow and instructions for example the Business Automation System
• Organization templates for example reports, biweekly meetings minutes,
etc.

text:
[Section 01: Effective Communication | Major Challenges in Communication]
Employees at GHD|EMPHNET are working through different interfaces such as
different departments, different organizations, country offices. Therefore, it is very
essential to understand major challenges that limit effective communication between
different interfaces at GHD|EMPHNET and to try to overcome. Many issues can arise
such as differences of opinion and miss-understandings. Involved employees need to
be aware of the differences , understand the divergences in attitudes between the
involved parties, and then act as intermediaries to facilitate communication.

General rules for using Microsoft Teams:
- Employees shall respond to received messages and calls immediately , if this
was not applicable, the user shall respond within 24 hours.
- Attendees shall be informed before recording any meeting.
- Opening cameras is mandatory in planned meetings.
- Meetings should be arranged using Outlook Meeting Requests:
o When organizing a meeting, check availability by viewing colleagues’
calendars or by using the Outlook Scheduling Assistant within a Meeting
Request.
o When you receive a meeting request, you should accept, reject , or
suggest a more suitable time  as soon as possible in order to help the
person arranging the meeting.
o Keep your Outlook calendar up -to-date by entering appointments and
holidays with the correct availability setting so others can check and see
your availability for meetings and collaborative work.
o Share your calendar with others to display your appointments. If you do
change the privacy setting to ‘None’ this will automatically be reverted to
Free/Busy.
o Share your calendar with your team so they can see your appointments.
o For part-time staff, create recurring appointments to show when you are
not normally working. If you normally finish work at 2:00 pm on a
Wednesday, set up a recurring appointment 2:00 – 5:30 pm every
Wednesday and set the availability to Out of Office with the subject ‘Non-
working time’.
o You may block out time to focus on a particular piece of work. This can be
marked as ‘Tentative’ so meeting organizers will try to avoid arranging
meetings during this time but may use it if there are no other options.

Face-to-face meeting is still the best communication as it is
direct and two-way communication and allows the
discussion of sensitive issues that require more nuance
derived from body language and direct interaction. It is the
ideal medium for holding discussions on important issues
and getting feedback from audience in an  immediate

more social aspects than many other forms.

or can be easily gathered in the same area , where body
language plays a vital role to deliver the message alongside
the direct interaction i.e. capacity building workshops,
interviews, etc.
